principles.title: Govern critical data elements, not everything
principles.statement: Only elements that drive regulatory returns, risk models, board KPIs or P&L are stewarded. Everything else is catalogued but not governed.
principles.rationale: A large bank holds on the order of a million columns and a few hundred elements that actually matter. Programmes that attempt full coverage exhaust their sponsor's patience before producing a measurable outcome.

principles.title: Derive scope backwards from consumption
principles.statement: Start at the regulatory return line or board KPI, trace lineage back to source, and every element on that path is in scope.
principles.rationale: Produces a finite, defensible list with immediate business relevance, and avoids an open-ended nomination process that never converges.

principles.title: Federated ownership, central standards
principles.statement: The DG Office sets standards, runs tooling and reports. Domains own their data, their definitions and their quality.
principles.rationale: Central-only models collapse at the throughput limit of the central team. Federation scales; centralisation queues.

principles.title: Accountability sits with the business, never with IT
principles.statement: Data Owners are business department heads. IT is custodian — it implements and secures, but does not decide what a term means or what quality is acceptable.
principles.rationale: When IT owns definitions, business disputes are unresolvable because the arbiter has no authority over the disputing parties.

principles.title: Enforcement over publication
principles.statement: Every policy must name at least one enforcement point — a pipeline test, an approval gate or a control — or it is not adopted.
principles.rationale: Unenforced policy documents are the most common artefact of failed programmes and the least useful.

principles.title: Stewardship time is explicit and contractual
principles.statement: Stewards are named individuals with a written percentage of time in their formal objectives, countersigned by their line manager.
principles.rationale: Unallocated stewardship is the single most reliable predictor of programme failure, and the easiest to eliminate before it happens.

principles.title: Every wave publishes a number
principles.statement: No wave completes without a measurable output — coverage, defect rate, issue closure or cost baseline.
principles.rationale: Governance is invisible until a number moves. Visible movement is what survives the next budget cycle.

roles.sitsIn: Executive committee — CFO, CRO or COO
accountableFor: Programme funding and reallocation of budget
Removing organisational blockers that the council cannot resolve
Holding Data Owners to their accountability at performance-review level
Chairing or attending the DG Council
roles.timeAllocation: Half a day per month, plus escalations
roles.failureMode: A sponsor with influence but no budget authority. Decisions bounce indefinitely; qualify this out before contracting.

accountableFor: Approving definitions for data elements in their domain
Setting acceptable quality thresholds and accepting residual risk
Approving access requests to their domain's data
Funding remediation of defects in their domain
Appointing and time-allocating stewards
roles.timeAllocation: Two to four hours per month; more during onboarding of their domain
roles.failureMode: Ownership assigned to whoever attended the workshop rather than whoever holds the budget and authority for the domain.

roles.sitsIn: Business — subject-matter expert within the domain
accountableFor: Authoring and maintaining glossary entries for their domain
Defining quality rules and thresholds with the custodian
Triaging and resolving data issues day to day
Maintaining the CDE register entries for their domain
Reviewing match exceptions and reference-data changes
roles.timeAllocation: Approximately 20% FTE, written into formal objectives
roles.failureMode: Stewardship added to an already-full role with no objective change. Queues stagnate within two months and the programme silently stops.

roles.sitsIn: Technology — platform, application or data engineering
accountableFor: Technical implementation of quality rules and controls
Storage, availability, backup and recovery
Implementing access entitlements as approved by the owner
Metadata harvesting and lineage capture from their systems
Executing remediation at the technical layer
roles.timeAllocation: Variable by wave; typically 10–20% during active onboarding of their system
roles.failureMode: Custodians treated as owners. Technology ends up arbitrating business definition disputes it has no authority to settle.

roles.sitsIn: Central — reporting to the CDO or sponsor
accountableFor: Standards, policies and the artefact set
Tooling operation and platform administration
Scorecard production and council secretariat
Facilitation, training and steward enablement
Programme reporting and benefit tracking
roles.timeAllocation: Full time — one to three people depending on estate size
roles.failureMode: The DG Office attempts to do stewardship itself to keep momentum. This works for one quarter and then becomes the bottleneck for everything.

roles.sitsIn: Cross-functional forum, chaired by the CDO or sponsor
accountableFor: Arbitrating definition and ownership disputes
Approving policies, standards and exceptions
Prioritising remediation and domain onboarding sequence
Reviewing the scorecard and holding owners to account
Escalating unresolved items to the executive committee
roles.timeAllocation: Monthly, ninety minutes, with quorum enforced
roles.failureMode: The council becomes a status meeting rather than a decision forum. If no decision is recorded in two consecutive meetings, it has failed.

roles.sitsIn: Central — executive or direct report to an executive
accountableFor: Data strategy and its alignment to the corporate strategy
Chairing the DG Council
Regulatory relationship on data matters
Investment prioritisation across the data agenda
roles.timeAllocation: Full time where the role exists; delivered as fractional advisory under the managed rung where it does not
roles.failureMode: The role exists on the organisation chart but carries no decision rights over domain budgets, making it advisory in practice.

accountableFor: Confirming which return line items and disclosures drive CDE scope
Validating backward lineage traces against submission logic
Signing off reconciliation rules between GL, subledger and source
Flagging regulatory change that alters governed element scope
roles.failureMode: Excluded from CDE derivation, so the resulting register reflects what technology thinks is reported rather than what is actually submitted.

accountableFor: Model input data requirements for credit, market and operational risk
Risk data aggregation completeness and timeliness expectations
IFRS 9 staging and provisioning input quality standards
Group and related-party exposure aggregation rules
roles.failureMode: Risk treats data quality as a modelling problem and absorbs defects into model overlays rather than escalating them for remediation at source.

accountableFor: KYC and CDD data completeness standards
Screening and transaction-monitoring input quality
Lineage defensibility for suspicious-activity reporting
Data-sharing and confidentiality constraint definition
roles.failureMode: Compliance data requirements arrive after the CDE register is closed, forcing a rework cycle mid-implementation.

raci.activity: Author and deploy a DQ rule
Onboard a new domain or system
Approve an AI or analytics use case for governed data

council.charterPurpose: To hold decision rights over enterprise data — definitions, ownership, quality standards, access and exceptions — at a level below the executive committee, so that data disputes are resolved by a competent forum rather than escalated to the CEO or left unresolved.
council.chair: Chief Data Officer, or the executive sponsor (CFO / CRO / COO) where no CDO exists
council.cadence: Monthly, ninety minutes, with papers circulated three working days in advance
council.quorum: The chair plus a majority of Data Owners. Attendance by delegate is permitted only where the delegate holds written decision authority.
members: Data Owners for each governed domain
Technology representative — head of data engineering or platform
decisionRights: Arbitrate contested business term definitions where owners disagree
Approve or reject additions to and removals from the CDE register
Approve policies, standards and the classification scheme
Grant, time-limit and review policy exceptions
Prioritise remediation of defects across competing domains
Set the sequence for domain and system onboarding
Gate AI and analytics use cases on data readiness
Escalate unresolved or under-resourced items to the executive committee
escalationPath: Steward attempts resolution within the domain, within SLA
Unresolved or cross-domain items go to the Data Owners concerned
Owner-level deadlock or resourcing conflict goes to the DG Council
Council-level deadlock, or any item requiring budget reallocation, goes to the executive sponsor
Matters with regulatory consequence go to the relevant board committee

gates.name: Sponsor authority confirmed
gates.test: The named sponsor can reallocate budget and can influence the performance objectives of prospective Data Owners. Influence without budget authority does not pass.

gates.name: Charter signed
gates.test: A DG charter is signed by the sponsor and records the council's decision rights explicitly.

gates.name: Data Owners named
gates.test: Every domain in scope has a named Data Owner at department-head level who has accepted the accountability in writing.

gates.name: Steward time allocated
gates.test: Each steward is named, has a written time percentage in their objectives, and their line manager has countersigned. This gate blocks the start of implementation.

gates.name: CDE register agreed
gates.test: The register is derived backwards from consumption, has an owner per element, and has been accepted by the council. Unassigned elements are recorded as open risks, not silently carried.

gates.name: Benefit baseline captured
gates.test: Pre-programme measurements exist for the metrics the business case claims will move. Retro-fitted baselines are not acceptable.

gates.name: Enforcement point identified per policy
gates.test: Each policy names at least one pipeline test, approval gate or control that enforces it. Policies with no enforcement point are flagged at council.

gates.name: Scorecard published
gates.test: A quality scorecard covering the governed CDEs is published and has been reviewed in at least one council meeting before the wave is accepted as complete.

gates.name: Issue workflow operating within SLA
gates.test: Real issues are being raised, triaged and closed within the agreed SLA, by stewards rather than by the delivery team.

gates.name: Handover independence demonstrated
gates.test: Stewards have run a full monthly cycle — scorecard review, triage, council attendance — without delivery-team intervention. Required before the retainer tier reduces.

gates.name: Metadata harvesting operating on schedule
gates.test: Harvest jobs for every in-scope system have completed on schedule for two consecutive cycles, and the catalogue reflects the current production schema rather than a point-in-time import.
